text: An embedding is a list of numbers (a vector) that represents the meaning of a piece of text. Texts with similar meaning end up with vectors that are close together.
A vector database stores embeddings and can quickly find the vectors closest to a query vector. Examples include pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate and Chroma.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors. A score near 1 means the texts point in the same direction in meaning; a score near 0 means they are unrelated.
Chunking splits long documents into smaller pieces before embedding them. Chunks that are too large dilute meaning; chunks that are too small lose context.
Chunk overlap repeats a few sentences between neighbouring chunks so that an idea split across a boundary is not lost.
BM25 is a keyword ranking algorithm. It scores documents by how often the query words appear, giving more weight to rare words and less to very long documents.
Hybrid search combines keyword search such as BM25 with embedding search, so exact terms and semantic meaning both count toward the final ranking.
Precision at k is the share of the top k retrieved documents that are actually relevant. Low precision means the context sent to the model contains noise.
Recall at k is the share of all relevant documents that appear in the top k results. Low recall means the model never sees information it needed.
Mean reciprocal rank (MRR) looks at the position of the first relevant result. A relevant document at rank 1 scores 1.0, at rank 2 scores 0.5, at rank 3 scores 0.33.
Reranking takes the first batch of retrieved documents and reorders them with a slower, more accurate model, usually a cross-encoder, before sending them to the LLM.
A hallucination is when a language model states something that is not supported by the retrieved context or by fact. Grounding answers in cited sources reduces it.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) first retrieves relevant documents for a question, then passes them to a language model as context so the answer is based on those sources.
Ragas is an evaluation library for RAG systems. It measures things like faithfulness to the context, answer relevance and context precision.
